RT by @no_itsmyturn: Mr. Kushner should judge Hamas by its actions, not its words. Since the ceasefire, Hamas and its allies have worked to consolidate their power in Gaza, signaling that they have no serious intention of fully disarming. Complete disarmament would amount to organizational suicide. It would also contradict the "muqawama" ideology at the core of Hamas’s identity. Armed "resistance groups" do not willingly surrender all their weapons, especially when threatened by potential conflict. Disarmament would also leave Hamas vulnerable to an Israeli effort to dismantle it or a challenge from rival anti-Hamas Palestinian factions such as the Popular Forces. Hamas did not survive the war only to relinquish power. Whatever its long-term plan may be, the group will not willingly surrender the military leverage that allows it to remain in control. Moreover, Hamas is not going to hand Netanyahu a significant political victory months before Israeli elections. That is why people should treat Hamas’s disarmament pledge with skepticism until Hamas and its allies disclose a detailed accounting of their entire arsenal in Gaza and submit the decommissioning process to credible independent verification. The IRA accepted independent verification more than two decades ago. Why should Hamas meet a lower standard? So far, Hamas and its allies have offered nothing comparable. @jaredkushner

Wildberries attack stats show 21 logistics sites hit with attacks, fires or evacuations from July 18 to August 16. The company has 209+ facilities totaling 5.6 million square meters, but 11 major complexes covering 1.38 million square meters were down by August 5th, nearly a quarter of all warehouse space. Not all 21 sites were directly hit, some just evacuated. Wildberries says the network keeps running by redirecting cargo, but each major facility knocked out strains the rest and complicates operations across Russia.
